title: PII Surface Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Student Privacy
Personally Identifiable Information
xAPI
Learning Record Store
Learning Analytics Ethics
description: A p5.js MicroSim that shows an illustrative xAPI statement one field per box. Learners classify each field as no PII risk, pseudonymous, direct identifier or uncontrolled free text, check their classes against Chapter 24's analysis (green match, amber defensible, red mismatch, each with a one-sentence reason), and compare the extra risks of Full LRS and LRS-Lite browser storage.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: The PII surface of an xAPI statement
learningObjectives: The learner will classify each field of an example xAPI statement as no PII risk, pseudonymous, direct identifier or uncontrolled free text, and explain what protects or exposes it.
prerequisites: The parts of an xAPI statement (Chapter 16)
The PII surface and pseudonymous versus anonymous (Chapter 24)

accessibility.notes: Fields can be selected with the arrow keys while the statement has focus and classified with the buttons or keys 1-4; verdicts use a symbol and a word as well as color; describe() lists every field and its current class; changes are announced in an aria-live region

controls.label: Statement fields
controls.purpose: Select the field to classify (click, or arrow keys when focused)

controls.label: No PII risk / Pseudonymous / Direct identifier / Uncontrolled free text
controls.purpose: Assign a class to the selected field

controls.label: Check my answers
controls.purpose: Color each classified field and show its reason

controls.label: Storage location
controls.purpose: List the extra risks of Full LRS or LRS-Lite browser storage

simulation.model: Rule-based comparison of learner classifications with the chapter's analysis
variables: class chosen for each of eight fields
assumptions: The statement and its values are fictional
The context.grouping and context.registration fields were added to the chapter's example for this exercise
Classes are the chapter's analysis, not a legal determination

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification with graded feedback (match, defensible, mismatch) and explanations
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Select a field, assign a class, check against an answer key
keyQuestions: Which single field brings personal identity into the statement?
Why is free text the least controllable part of the surface?
What new risk appears when statements are stored in the browser?
commonMisconceptions: A code such as student-4471 is anonymous
A pseudonym is the same as anonymity
Pseudonymizing the actor removes every identity from a stored statement
assessmentOpportunities: Number of fields matched or defended
Written reason for each amber field
Comparison of Full LRS and LRS-Lite risks
